episodes.205553: Isolated strong to severe thunderstorms developed during the late afternoon, producing isolated wind damage and small hail.
episodes.205648: An upper level low moved over the Intermountain West on September 12th. This along with an upper level high over Texas allowed monsoon moisture to stream north into western and central New Mexico during these days resulting in numerous to widespread showers and thunderstorms. Strong winds at the leading edge of a line of thunderstorms moving into the Albuquerque Metro resulted in a 58 mph wind gust on the West Mesa of Albuquerque.
episodes.205657: A severe thunderstorm moved through Sheridan county with severe hail.
episodes.205714: A thunderstorm tracked from north central to southwest Corson county on September 12th, with hail to the size of golf balls observed about 10 miles south of Morristown.
episodes.206317: An upper-level trough produced afternoon showers and thunderstorms. A weak CAPE profile kept the severe thunderstorm risk on the low end. However, with the upper-level low overhead with embedded mini vorticity maximums, a brief landspout was able to form.
episodes.207260: A large thunderstorm to the north of a warm front moved across the Brainerd Lakes area during the morning of the 12th. The storm produced quite a bit of hail, with the largest to the size of ping pong balls. In some locations, there was so much hail covering the ground it looked like snow.
episodes.207385: Northeast sea breeze flow coupled with troughing aloft over the eastern U.S. extending south into the Florida peninsula lead to late afternoon thunderstorms that produce a waterspout offshore North Fort Myers Beach in Lee County.
episodes.207413: Showers developed along the Colorado/Kansas border with showers spreading into Hamilton county. There an AWOS recorded a severe wind gust. This is likely due to a dry microburst generated by evaporative cooling. That report was the only one near severe thresholds and appears to be localized to a small area.
episodes.207507: A thunderstorm developed in the lee of the Bighorns and became severe as it moved eastward. A trained spotter reported quarter-sized hail to the southeast of Buffalo.
episodes.207517: A boundary stretching east from a surface low pressure system in northwest North Dakota combined with the northern tip of a low level jet to produce thunderstorms over north central North Dakota. Some of these storms became severe producing large hail. The largest hail was two inches in diameter, and fell near Granville in McHenry County.
episodes.207518: A surface low pressure system was located over central South Dakota while multiple short-wave troughs moved through southwesterly flow aloft. This led to multiple areas of thunderstorms developing, with some becoming severe. Initially, a storm became severe near Fessenden in Wells County in the morning, producing one inch diameter hail.  Then in the early afternoon, another thunderstorm produced a brief tornado near Wheelock in Williams County. The tornado touched down in an open field and impacted no structures, therefore there was no damage to evaluate. By National Weather Service policy the tornado is rated EF-U (Unknown).  Later in the afternoon into the evening, additional thunderstorms became severe over southwest North Dakota. The largest hail reported was the size of a ping pong ball, which fell at Solen in Sioux County.
episodes.207549: Showers and thunderstorms originating in weak, nebulous lower to middle tropospheric steering flow on the afternoon of September 12, 2025, produced isolated gale force wind gusts and a waterspout near the Lower Florida Keys.  The showers and thunderstorms eventually evolved into a mesoscale convective system over the southeast Gulf of America featuring a large southward-moving outflow boundary bringing scattered gale-force wind gusts through much of the Florida Keys coastal waters the evening of September 12 to the early morning hours of September 13, 2025.
episodes.207568: The presence of a deep layered trough fired up showers across the local waters. One of these showers manage to develop a waterspout, that was observed and recorded from the Guanica boardwalk.
episodes.207593: Persistent shower activity was observed as a tropical wave moves across the local area. This moisture, along with a weak steering flow, resulted in the development of strong thunderstorms across the interior of Puerto Rico.
episodes.207655: A very active monsoon period occurred September 12th and September 13th across Southeastern Arizona. Strong to severe thunderstorms began in the late morning on September 12th and continued through the overnight hours of September 13th. Severe thunderstorms were able to produce hail ranging from 1 inch to an estimated 2.75 inches in diameter and measured wind gusts of 60 to 63 mph. Thunderstorm winds caused a semi-truck driving on Interstate 10 to be overturned, with no injury. Additionally, a landspout tornado near Vail, Arizona was reported with no injury or damage to property. Heavy rainfall due to thunderstorm activity led to water running over washes and roadways causing the death of an individual in Benson, AZ in a swift water rescue. Additionally, the running water caused damage to roadways in Benson, AZ.
episodes.207695: Thunderstorms moving offshore produced strong wind gusts at the coast.
episodes.207721: Pulse convection and thunderstorms produced localized areas of nearly stationary, intense rainfall and hail ranging from pea sized to 1 inch in diameter during the afternoon and evening of September 11th.
episodes.207727: The period between the 11th and 13th of September had a relatively unique meteorological setup for western Colorado and eastern Utah. A potent closed low was located over Southern California, and a ridge of high pressure was located to our southeast, directing a rich plume of monsoonal moisture northward through the Four Corners. Mixing ratios in this plume of moisture were more than high enough to not only help form strong to severe thunderstorms, but also to produce flash flooding and debris flows. Additionally, there was ample instability, with morning clearing helping 600-1000 J/kg of CAPE develop each afternoon. The region also fell under the right exit region of a potent upper level jet streak, which added additional lift and 40-50 kts of shear. Additionally, terrain effects added additional lift and shear. All together, this was a potent setup with the potential to produce severe thunderstorms. And indeed, the storms that developed produced not only large hail and strong, damaging winds, but also two tornadoes in Southeast Utah, and flash flooding across the area. Particularly, fresh burn scars, including the Lee and Elk RBX scars, saw substantial flash flooding and debris flows as storms trained over the area and produced very heavy rain. Finally, after 3 days of widespread severe weather, the cold front pushed through the region, and a cooler, drier, and above all, calmer airmass moved in, bringing an end to the event.

episodes.207781: A surface boundary over Central Florida with influence from a mid level shortwave trough led to diurnal showers and thunderstorms developing over Southeast Florida on the 11th and 12th of September.
episodes.207803: Elevated thunderstorms brought a round of overnight hail in the early morning hours with several reports of quarter to golf ball sized stones occurring.
episodes.207820: A couple storms were strong enough to produce marginally severe weather with a 1 inch hail report and another producing some wind damage.
episodes.208341: A few thunderstorms developed across the Black Hills during the late afternoon and evening and produced a few one inch hail reports and a strong wind gust.

AWOS station K3K3 Syracuse recorded a 59 mph wind gust.

The Idaho County Sheriff's Office Facebook page reported washouts and subsequent closure on Reservation Line Road near Cottonwood Creek due to heavy rainfall from thunderstorms. A Flood Advisory for the area was issued on the evening of the 11th. The Sheriff's office reported that the road reopened by 1320 PST on the 12th.
Social media report - Time estimated via radar. Handful of nickel to quarter sized hail with one larger stone of at least half dollar size.
Social media report of hail up 1.25 inches.

events.narrative: A northwest wind of 37 knots was recorded at the National Ocean Service gauge at the Florida Keys National Marine Sanctuary's Nancy Foster Center.
At 806 MST on September 12, an NWS employee reported 1 inch diameter hail 25 miles NNW of Castle Valley, Utah. Some hail stones a little bigger than one inch fell.
Hail was accumulating and looked like snow.
At 844 MST on September 12, law enforcement reported 1.25 inch diameter hail 17 miles NW of Moab, Utah.
At 908 MST on September 12, a CoCoRaHS observer reported 0.75 inch diameter hail 5 miles NW of Mack, Colorado.
Law Enforcement reported standing water on Interstate 70 near Cisco, UT due to heavy rain from passing thunderstorms.

Multiple photos of landspout tornado near a remote area of the Rincon Mountains near Vail, AZ. The tornado occurred in a remote area that would be difficult to survey. Tornado path and width estimated.  No damage or injury reported.

events.county: Gulf Of America From West End Of Seven Mile Bridge To Halfmoon Shoal Out To 5 Fathoms
events.narrative: A narrow, vertical waterspout with an observed spray ring was reported approximately four miles north northwest of the Niles Channel Bridge.  The waterspout was observed for a few minutes before it became tilted and more rope-like before dissipating.
At 1024 MST on September 12, public reported 0.75 inch diameter hail in Moab, Utah.

The CoCoRaHS reported at Mack 5NW called in a report of a 61 mph wind gust at her location in association with a passing thunderstorm. No reports of injuries, damages, or fatalities were received in association with this event.
The tornado touched down in an open field southeast of Wheelock and impacted no structures. There was no damage to evaluate. By National Weather Service policy the tornado is rated EF-U (Unknown).
Several photos and videos showing quarter size hail in San Manuel.
Photo of 1 inch hail in Benson, AZ.
Photo and video of numerous 1 inch hail stones.
Local broadcast media and emergency management reported flooding along Arthur Street in Hollywood with the road submerged in water.

Public reported flooding across State Highway 139 south of Douglas Pass due to several rounds of heavy rain training over the steep and saturated terrain. No reports of road closures or damages to the roadway.

events.county: Hawk Channel From Ocean Reef To Craig Key Out To The Reef
events.narrative: A northwest wind gust of 35 knots was recorded at a WeatherFlow station at Carysfort Reef Light.
Emergency managers report a landslide affecting both lanes of Road 111 at km 55.2, near Papin Grocery Store and Bar in Utuado.
A member of the public posted an image on social media of a fallen power pole struck by  lightning during thunderstorm activity in Bo. Saltos, Sector La Charca in Orocovis.

Report via media: Funnel cloud was observed picking up dust for about 45 seconds and believed to have touched the ground. Location was about 6 mi south of Buffalo and 2 mi west of Garneill. No damages were reported with the landspout.

At 2:30 PM MDT, the mesonet site US-191 at MP 104 Flat Iron recorded a wind gust to 60 mph in association with a passing thunderstorm. Other sensors in the area recorded wind gusts of 45-55 mph in association with the same storm. No reports of damages, injuries, or fatalities were received in association with this storm.
Kane Creek Boulevard/Kane Springs Road and Potash Road reported as impassable due to flooding and mud on the roadways.

Emergency managers report runoff and flooding on Road 111, in front of LarCoop near Residencial Jardines de Utuado and the Emergency Management office. Roads remain  passable, with about 3 inches of rainfall were recorded at the time of the report.
National Park Service employees at Arches National Park reported Cache Valley Road had washed out near the lower Delicate Arch viewpoint.

At 3:06 PM MDT, NWS Grand Junction received a report from local law enforcement that powerlines had been downed in nearby Fruita, CO in association with a passing severe thunderstorm. Six minutes later, this storm reached the Grand Junction Regional Airport, where the KGJT ASOS recorded a wind gust to 68 mph. No other damages were reported with this event, and no reports of injuries or fatalities were received.
Law Enforcement reported a debris flow that closed County Road 5 due to heavy rain on the recent Lee Burn Scar.

National Park Service employees based at Chimney Rock National Monument reported flash flooding on State Route 151 between Pagosa Springs and Arboles. Additionally, washouts and debris were reported in the Chimney Rock National Monument itself, with the LSR reading Upper road and parking lots impassable. Chimney Rock National Monument had to be closed the following day (September 13th, 2025) to clear debris.

Utah Department of Transportation traffic cameras indicated flooding/ponding of water at the intersection of US Highway 191 and State Route 128, north of the town of Moab. This was due primarily to heavy rainfall on already saturate soils. Impacts were minimal and once the rain stopped, the roadway cleared.

A trained spotter reported street flooding at the intersection of State Route 340 and Rimrock Drive, near the west entrance to Colorado National Monument. No reports of road closures or damages due to this flooding were received.

A 58 mph wind gust was observed on the West Mesa of Albuquerque along the leading edge of a line of thunderstorms.
